mechanism: EXPAND-MULTIPATH-DESCRIPTOR (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:1004-1030) works on the raw STRING: it strips the checksum, takes the FIRST <...> group, and if any further #\< appears anywhere in the remaining body it signals "Multiple multipath key path specifiers found" (:1023). Its own docstring states the rule it enforces -- "Core allows at most ONE multipath specifier per descriptor" (:1012) -- and that statement about Core is false. In Core that error lives INSIDE ParseKeyPath (refs/bitcoin/src/script/descriptor.cpp:1808-1810) and fires only when ONE key expression carries two specifiers. Across key expressions ParseScript collects one provider vector per key, computes max_providers_len, clones every length-1 vector up to it, and errors only on a length that is neither 1 nor the max: "multi(): Multipath derivation paths have mismatched lengths" (descriptor.cpp:2374-2384); the same clone-and-length-match appears for musig() (:2049-2078) and for miniscript (:2646). Core's own vectors pin this: descriptor_tests.cpp:748 checks multi(2,xprv.../<1;2>/*,xprv.../<3;4>/0/*) VALID, and :803 checks a three-key sh(multi(...)) with two different specifiers of length 3 plus one plain key VALID. Second, independent half of the same root cause: because the expander does not know the grammar, it also substitutes a specifier that sits inside an ORIGIN, where Core passes allow_multipath=false (descriptor.cpp:2134) and refuses outright -- so the same function BOTH refuses valid descriptors and accepts invalid ones. Refuter checks that FAILED to refute it: (1) it is not a checksum artefact -- the failure is reached on the raw body before any checksum work; (2) it is not confined to deriveaddresses -- importdescriptors reaches the same expander at src/wallet/wallet.lisp:2173, and because that call site swallows the rpc-error (handler-case ... (bl.rpc:rpc-error () nil)) the request then falls through to parse-descriptor and reports the WRONG message, "Multi: Multipath descriptors are not supported", instead of the expander's; (3) an ordinary hand-written workaround does exist (import the /0/* and /1/* forms as two separate descriptors), which is what keeps this off the funds bar.
consequence: S2: the standard n-of-m cosigner export -- wsh(sortedmulti(2,xpubA/<0;1>/*,xpubB/<0;1>/*)), the shape Core, Sparrow, BDK and Ledger Live write -- is refused by every entry point we have, including the two that DO support single-specifier multipath. A user restoring a multisig wallet from its BIP389 backup is told the descriptor is invalid, with an error text that does not name the real limitation. The workaround (hand-expand into two descriptors and import each with the right internal flag) exists and is what Core's expansion produces anyway, so no funds are stuck -- this is a valid descriptor refused plus a wrong answer an operator acts on. The mirror-image half is worse than a refusal but still bounded: importdescriptors ACCEPTED wpkh([deadbeef/<0;1>]tpub.../0/*), which Core rejects, and imported it as two active descriptors carrying fabricated distinct origins ([deadbeef/0/0] and [deadbeef/1/1]) whose scriptPubKeys are IDENTICAL, so the wallet's change chain reuses its receive addresses -- a privacy defect and a wallet Core would never have created, not a loss of funds.

fix_shape: Do not patch the string expander to count specifiers per key expression -- delete it, and let the parser own multipath, which is the same fix 232c293f needs and the only one that gets the origin case right. Concretely: %PARSE-KEY-PATH gains Core's ParseKeyPath contract (descriptor.cpp:1789-1851) -- it already receives ALLOW-MULTIPATH, so an origin keeps refusing while a key path expands; it records one placeholder plus the substitute values, signals "Multiple multipath key path specifiers found" only when a SECOND specifier appears in the SAME key expression, and returns a list of key paths. Each key expression then yields a vector of desc-keys, %PARSE-DESCRIPTOR-BODY takes max_providers_len over the key expressions of one script, clones every length-1 vector up to it and otherwise signals "<fn>(): Multipath derivation paths have mismatched lengths" with the function-name prefix Core uses (multi/musig/Miniscript, descriptor.cpp:2384, 2078, 2646), and PARSE-DESCRIPTOR returns the descriptor list. importdescriptors and deriveaddresses then consume that list instead of EXPAND-MULTIPATH-DESCRIPTOR, and %PROCESS-MULTIPATH-IMPORT keeps its second-expansion-is-internal rule. Port Core's CheckMultipath vectors (descriptor_tests.cpp:748 and :803) as the oracle, and add two negative controls that today pass for the wrong reason: the mismatched-lengths case must report Core's message, and the origin case wpkh([deadbeef/<0;1>]xpub/0/*) must be REFUSED by importdescriptors, not imported as two descriptors.
